policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Apply the memory update before choosing the next subgoal. Give holding a cube priority: if a cube is held, choose C, place the cube onto the table. Otherwise, if remaining_targets is None and no completed reveal is available, choose A, press button. When remaining_targets is a nonempty list and the gripper is empty, choose B, pick up the highlighted cube, targeting an unpicked member of remaining_targets. Follow any pickup priority explicitly supplied by the goal instruction or current observations; absent such a priority, any remaining member is admissible. Serialization order does not establish pickup priority. Point at that cube's current center, allowing minor centroid wobble; do not point at the former white area or substitute another cube of the same color.  If the current scene shows a cube held after pickup, choose C, place the cube onto the table, even though that cube has already been removed from remaining_targets. After placement, an empty gripper and a nonempty remaining_targets list lead back to B for an unpicked member selected by the same rule; never pick up an already removed cube again. If pickup failed, retain the target and retry B. If placement failed and the cube remains held, retry C. If the target is temporarily occluded, use its stored table coordinate for B rather than switching targets. If remaining_targets is empty and the gripper is empty, the task is complete; no further pickup or button press is required. If nevertheless forced to select a menu option after completion, choose C as the non-pickup fallback. For other unmodeled situations, choose C if holding a cube, otherwise B at a remaining target selected by the same rule if one exists, otherwise A only when remaining_targets is None.

fields.name: remaining_targets
fields.description: Treat an empty incoming memory, a missing or blank remaining_targets field, or None as uninitialized. Write the literal sentinel None if no button reveal is available; never leave the field blank or write null. Inspect all execution frames provided at this decision, not just the final scene. If the field is uninitialized and the frames show the button-press interval and white highlighted areas, associate each highlighted area with the cube immediately above or overlapping it and record that cube's table center as [y, x]. Deduplicate repeated sightings. Order targets by image columns from smaller x to larger x; cubes whose x coordinates differ by at most 10 pixels count as the same column and are ordered by increasing y. This is a serialization convention only, not a pickup priority. Once initialized, retain this list. If the supplied frames show a cube being grasped at a listed table location and subsequently lifted while held, remove that entry at this decision. Use its pre-lift table position to identify it, not its raised position. An unsuccessful closure, temporary disappearance, or observation of an already-held cube is not sufficient for removal. Placement neither removes an entry nor adds one back. Preserve an occluded remaining target while another cube is released. Keep stored coordinates unchanged despite occlusion or small visible centroid changes. Write [] only after all revealed targets have actually been picked up; None means the reveal has not yet been recorded. e.g. [[63, 150]]
